approach: Willow Lake/South Crestone trailhead at about 8,950 ft above Crestone. South Crestone Lake Trail #860 runs 4.4 mi to the lake at 11,800 ft. The tower sits short of the big meadow, part way up, at a mileage no source gives. Likely 1-2 hr, but unverified.
summit: A tower top on a forested hillside, not the summit or ridge crest of a peak. Descent scrambles into a notch.
reason: No source found gives the distance to the meadow, and a hillside tower top on its own reads as crag-like, so neither test is met with confidence. Settle it by measuring trail miles from the trailhead to the meadow: under about 2.5 mi means trad.

approach: The W is Peak 6856 on BLM land just outside Bighorn National Forest, near Shell on the west slope of the Bighorn Mountains. Brokeback Mountain is behind it. The approach takes the Dry Horse Creek trail to the saddle between Wet Horse and Dry Horse creeks, then goes west off-trail to the Eocene tower. No source gives a time or distance. One trail listing gives about 2.5 mi (3.96 km) for a 'Dry Horse Trail', but its elevations (1,445-1,633 m) sit well below the 6,586 ft tower, so it may not be the same approach.
summit: Ends on the tower summit. Mountain Project lists Brokeback Mountain at 6,586 ft and calls it technically its own summit separate from The W. Descent is by rappel.
reason: Topping out on a named summit points to alpine, but this is a low foothill tower more like a crag summit, and the approach length is unconfirmed, so the call stays open (leaning alpine if the approach runs well over an hour). Settle it with the Dry Horse trailhead's elevation and the mileage to the saddle.

approach: The same approach as Dead Horse Road: the Dry Horse Creek trail to the Wet Horse/Dry Horse saddle behind The W near Shell, WY, then west along the ridge to the Eocene tower. Mountain Project gives no time or distance.
summit: Tops out on the Eocene tower, which seems to be the high point of Brokeback Mountain (6,586 ft). Rappel back to the ground.
reason: It is the same formation and the same unknown approach as Dead Horse Road, so it should get the same call. Treat the two together once the approach length is known.

approach: Park at Zopkios rest area and walk about 1 km along Hwy 5, then follow a cairned climbers' trail: about 30-40 min and about 300 m gain to the base. A trip report timed 35 min from car to base.
summit: Summit at about 2,039-2,040 m (6,690 ft), with about 500 m prominence. The slab routes finish with a scramble to the summit area. One trip report notes a slightly higher summit point beyond where the route tops out, so they end near the true summit but not always on it. The descent walks off on a trail around the north side, about 1-1.5 hr back to the car.
reason: The approach is short, but the routes climb about 500 m of a named granite peak to its summit area and descend over the mountain, which meets the summit test and the owner's rule that a peak's 5th-class route is alpine. Mountain Project tags the classics Trad and Alpine and says the short approach draws alpine climbers. One local trip report does stress how close it is to the highway, so it is a roadside alpine objective rather than a crag.

approach: Confirmed for Green Giant Buttress: about 3 mi and 1,500 ft from the end of the Clear Creek road (FR 2065), taking about 2 hr. One party timed 1:45 from the road end and 2:15 from a blowdown-blocked car. The approach is off-trail in the Boulder River Wilderness: an old mining road, a Copper Creek fork crossing, gullies, and a 3rd-class slab scramble to the staging area. Note that Desire is on the separate Comb Buttress (Squire Creek side, approach reported from 20 min in the guidebook to about 1 hr of bushwhacking), not on Green Giant.
summit: Neither. Dreamer officially ends at bolted anchors on the face at about pitch 9-10, and the top of the buttress is one extra grungy pitch above. Parties rappel the route to the base, about 9-10 double-rope raps.
reason: The routes end on the face and rappel to the base like a crag, so only the approach makes this alpine: about 2 hr of off-trail wilderness travel, beyond the 1-hour crag limit, makes it borderline alpine. Desire, if it is really on Comb Buttress with a shorter approach, should be rechecked and could be trad.
